args.content:
Halcyon Threshold

Contributing to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

What this is

Halcyon Threshold is an independent effort to do useful work on AI safety and governance. The field has more newsletters than replications, more launches than sustained contributions. We aim to be different: pick one narrow thing and do it well.

Current focus

  • Independent replication — Verifying published safety results so the field can trust its foundations.
  • Agent evaluations — Building practical tests for autonomous agents acting with broad capabilities.
  • Operations support — Providing engineering and compute help to small research groups that need it.

Principles

  • Small, checkable contributions beat big launches.
  • Talk to five people doing adjacent work before building.
  • Do not announce before you have something to show.
  • Negative results are as valuable as positive ones.

Contact

Morgan Hale — morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Halcyon Threshold is a personal project. No external funding accepted at this time.

For now, Halcyon Threshold is staying focused on narrow technical contributions — replication, evaluations, and operations support for researchers — rather than public advocacy. We're following the principle: small, checkable contributions beat big launches.

Best of luck with the letter.

Halcyon Threshold

args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out. Here's what I can offer:

"I started Halcyon Threshold because the AI safety field has more newsletters than replications, more launches than sustained contributions. The labs are optimizing for capability; someone needs to optimize for reliability — verifying that safety techniques actually work, building evaluations for autonomous agents, and giving small research groups the engineering support they need to iterate. Grand declarations don't make systems safer. Careful, checkable work does."

Feel free to attribute to Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold. Happy to expand if you need more.

Best,
Morgan

args.subject: Re: Offer of help
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for the offer — that's genuinely kind.

Right now the three things Halcyon Threshold is focused on:

1. **Independent replication** — Re-running published safety experiments to verify results. Needs: someone who can read papers carefully, set up environments, run code, document discrepancies.

2. **Agent evaluations** — Building practical test suites for autonomous agents. Needs: designing scenarios, writing evaluation scripts, analyzing results.

3. **Operations support** — Helping small research groups with engineering/compute. Needs: setting up infra, debugging pipelines, managing compute credits.

If any of those sound interesting, we could do a quick call this week to find a concrete slice that fits ~5 hours/week. No pressure either way.

Best,
Morgan

args.content:
# Emberfall Rapid Grant Proposal: Independent Replication & Agent Evaluations

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (Halcyon Threshold)
**Date:** 16 November 2026
**Requested amount:** $15,000

---

## What we'll do

**Independent Replication Pipeline (8 weeks)**
- Identify 5–8 high-impact AI safety papers from 2023–2025 with published code but no independent replication
- Re-run experiments in clean environments, document all discrepancies
- Publish replication reports (positive or negative) on Alignment Commons and GitHub
- Build a reusable replication template: environment specs, compute requirements, common failure modes

**Agent Evaluation Suite (8 weeks, parallel)**
- Design 20+ practical evaluation scenarios for autonomous agents (tool use, delegation, long-horizon planning, recovery from errors)
- Implement as runnable test suites compatible with major agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGPT-style, custom)
- Run evaluations against 3–4 open-weight models; publish results and methodology
- Release evaluation framework for community use

---

## Why us / why Morgan

- 3 years as ML engineer at a mid-sized AI company (production systems, not research)
- Organized the local AI safety reading group for 18 months; knows the literature and the people
- Halcyon Threshold principles: narrow scope, checkable outputs, no announcements before results
- No institutional overhead — every dollar goes to compute, tooling, and contractor hours (e.g., Priya Raman, data analyst, 5 hrs/week for replication runs)

---

## Budget

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Cloud compute (GPU hours for replication runs + evals) | $7,000 |
| Contractor: Priya Raman (5 hrs/week × 16 weeks × $50/hr) | $4,000 |
| Tooling/infrastructure (eval framework hosting, CI, storage) | $2,000 |
| Contingency / buffer | $2,000 |
| **Total** | **$15,000** |

---

## Deliverables (by end of grant period)

1. **5–8 replication reports** — each with: original claim, reproduction steps, results, discrepancies, root-cause analysis
2. **Agent evaluation framework** — open-source, documented, with 20+ scenarios and baseline results on 3–4 models
3. **Public write-ups** on Alignment Commons for each replication and the evaluation framework
4. **Replication guide** — a practical template for others to replicate safety work

---

## Accountability

Morgan Hale is the named applicant and will be personally accountable for all deliverables. Progress updates available biweekly. All code and data open-sourced under MIT/CC-BY.
